findings.issue: pkill -f patterns matched the agent's own bash -c command line twice, killing its own shell (exit 143) and forcing re-diagnosis each time
findings.suggestion: Kill by explicit PID from ps output, or use pkill patterns that cannot appear in the shell's own argv (e.g. `pkill -f '^node .*server'` with anchors)

findings.issue: Stale app process held port 3200 and served the old build, producing a false 'No Pokémon found' regression and a wasted screenshot/diagnosis cycle
findings.suggestion: After any background start, check the log for EADDRINUSE and confirm the new PID is the one listening before treating a symptom as a code regression

findings.issue: First manual server start was a garbled command (literal 'node server-placeholder', three conflicting port numbers), leaving ambiguous process state
findings.suggestion: Start servers with one clean nohup + pidfile per command, one port per process, and verify each with a curl before proceeding

findings.issue: Heredoc missing its NODE terminator, producing a bash warning (script did still execute)
findings.suggestion: Verify heredoc terminators, or write screenshot scripts to a temp file instead of inline heredocs in long compound commands

findings.issue: Wrote a known-suspect typesToFetch helper that over-fetched 3 excluded types; caught in self-review but only removed 30 turns later
findings.suggestion: Fix self-identified dead code at write time rather than deferring; it added avoidable latency to every index build

summary: A disciplined, well-planned build: requirements validated against real data before coding, a single root-caused fix cycle, and thorough verification including post-final-edit test runs and visual comparison against the reference screenshots. The only real weakness is background-process bookkeeping — two self-killing pkill calls and a stale server that manufactured a false regression and cost roughly nine turns. Would merge the process habits of this agent into any team.
